claims.title: Founding of Great Moravia
claims.summary: Prince Mojmír I expelled Pribina of Nitra and united the principalities of Moravia and Nitra into Great Moravia, the first powerful Slavic state of central Europe, with the Slovak lands at its core.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Slovakia: From Great Moravia to the heart of Europe, a nation that waited a thousand years for its own state.", terralore.co/country/SVK/chronicle#ev-833-founding-of-great-moravia, claim TL:SVK:event:833:founding-of-great-moravia, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Mission of Cyril and Methodius
claims.summary: At Prince Rostislav's request the Byzantine brothers Cyril and Methodius arrived in Great Moravia, devised the Glagolitic script and translated the liturgy into Old Church Slavonic, founding a written Slavic culture.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Slovakia: From Great Moravia to the heart of Europe, a nation that waited a thousand years for its own state.", terralore.co/country/SVK/chronicle#ev-863-mission-of-cyril-and-methodius, claim TL:SVK:event:863:mission-of-cyril-and-methodius, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Reign of Svatopluk I
claims.summary: Under Svatopluk I Great Moravia reached its greatest extent and won recognition from the papacy, becoming the dominant power of the middle Danube before the state fragmented after his death.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Slovakia: From Great Moravia to the heart of Europe, a nation that waited a thousand years for its own state.", terralore.co/country/SVK/chronicle#ev-870-reign-of-svatopluk-i, claim TL:SVK:event:870:reign-of-svatopluk-i, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Fall of Great Moravia to the Magyars
claims.summary: Weakened by internal strife and Frankish wars, Great Moravia collapsed as the Magyars occupied the Carpathian Basin; a Magyar victory in 906–907 is taken to mark the end of the state.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Slovakia: From Great Moravia to the heart of Europe, a nation that waited a thousand years for its own state.", terralore.co/country/SVK/chronicle#ev-907-fall-of-great-moravia-to-the-magyars, claim TL:SVK:event:907:fall-of-great-moravia-to-the-magyars, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Incorporation into the Kingdom of Hungary
claims.summary: The Slovak lands were absorbed into the Kingdom of Hungary founded by Stephen I, beginning roughly a thousand years under the Hungarian crown as the region known as 'Upper Hungary'.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Slovakia: From Great Moravia to the heart of Europe, a nation that waited a thousand years for its own state.", terralore.co/country/SVK/chronicle#ev-1000-incorporation-into-the-kingdom-of-hungary, claim TL:SVK:event:1000:incorporation-into-the-kingdom-of-hungary, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Universitas Istropolitana at Pressburg
claims.summary: Slovakia's first university, the Universitas Istropolitana, was founded at Pressburg, an early sign of the towns' wealth and learning within the Hungarian kingdom.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Slovakia: From Great Moravia to the heart of Europe, a nation that waited a thousand years for its own state.", terralore.co/country/SVK/chronicle#ev-1467-universitas-istropolitana-at-pressburg, claim TL:SVK:event:1467:universitas-istropolitana-at-pressburg, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Pressburg made capital of Hungary
claims.summary: As the Ottomans overran central Hungary, the parliament promoted Pressburg (now Bratislava) to capital of the Kingdom of Hungary, a secure stronghold close to Habsburg Vienna.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Slovakia: From Great Moravia to the heart of Europe, a nation that waited a thousand years for its own state.", terralore.co/country/SVK/chronicle#ev-1536-pressburg-made-capital-of-hungary, claim TL:SVK:event:1536:pressburg-made-capital-of-hungary, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Pressburg the coronation city
claims.summary: Between 1563 and 1830, eleven Hungarian kings and eight royal consorts were crowned at St Martin's Cathedral in Pressburg, including Maria Theresa in 1741, making the city the ceremonial heart of the kingdom.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Slovakia: From Great Moravia to the heart of Europe, a nation that waited a thousand years for its own state.", terralore.co/country/SVK/chronicle#ev-1563-pressburg-the-coronation-city, claim TL:SVK:event:1563:pressburg-the-coronation-city, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Bernolák's first written Slovak
claims.summary: The Catholic priest Anton Bernolák codified an early written Slovak based on western dialects, an opening move in the national awakening that the next generation would supersede.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Slovakia: From Great Moravia to the heart of Europe, a nation that waited a thousand years for its own state.", terralore.co/country/SVK/chronicle#ev-1787-bernolak-s-first-written-slovak, claim TL:SVK:event:1787:bernolak-s-first-written-slovak, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Štúr codifies literary Slovak
claims.summary: Ľudovít Štúr and his associates resolved to base a unified Slovak literary language on the central Slovak dialects; his standard, refined by later grammarians, became modern literary Slovak.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Slovakia: From Great Moravia to the heart of Europe, a nation that waited a thousand years for its own state.", terralore.co/country/SVK/chronicle#ev-1843-stur-codifies-literary-slovak, claim TL:SVK:event:1843:stur-codifies-literary-slovak, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Magyarization under the Compromise
claims.summary: After the Austro-Hungarian Compromise the Hungarian government intensified Magyarization, pressing the Magyar language on Slovak schools and public life and denying the Slovaks recognition as a nation.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Slovakia: From Great Moravia to the heart of Europe, a nation that waited a thousand years for its own state.", terralore.co/country/SVK/chronicle#ev-1867-magyarization-under-the-compromise, claim TL:SVK:event:1867:magyarization-under-the-compromise, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Slovaks in the revolutions of 1848
claims.summary: During the revolutions of 1848 Slovak leaders, Štúr among them, set out national demands and raised volunteers, asserting the Slovaks as a distinct people within the Hungarian kingdom.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Slovakia: From Great Moravia to the heart of Europe, a nation that waited a thousand years for its own state.", terralore.co/country/SVK/chronicle#ev-1848-slovaks-in-the-revolutions-of-1848, claim TL:SVK:event:1848:slovaks-in-the-revolutions-of-1848, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Czechoslovakia and the Martin Declaration
claims.summary: Czechoslovakia was declared in Prague on 28 October 1918; on 30 October the Slovak National Council endorsed the union in the Martin Declaration, giving the Slovaks their first modern statehood alongside the Czechs.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Slovakia: From Great Moravia to the heart of Europe, a nation that waited a thousand years for its own state.", terralore.co/country/SVK/chronicle#ev-1918-czechoslovakia-and-the-martin-declaration, claim TL:SVK:event:1918:czechoslovakia-and-the-martin-declaration, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Proclamation of the Slovak State
claims.summary: As Germany dismembered Czechoslovakia, a separate Slovak State was proclaimed under the priest Jozef Tiso, a clerical-authoritarian regime that became a client and ally of Nazi Germany.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Slovakia: From Great Moravia to the heart of Europe, a nation that waited a thousand years for its own state.", terralore.co/country/SVK/chronicle#ev-1939-proclamation-of-the-slovak-state, claim TL:SVK:event:1939:proclamation-of-the-slovak-state, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Deportation of Slovak Jews
claims.summary: Slovakia became the first Axis partner to consent to the deportation of its Jews; between March and October 1942 some 57,000 Slovak Jews were deported to German-occupied Poland, with more than 60,000 of Slovakia's Jews murdered overall.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Slovakia: From Great Moravia to the heart of Europe, a nation that waited a thousand years for its own state.", terralore.co/country/SVK/chronicle#ev-1942-deportation-of-slovak-jews, claim TL:SVK:event:1942:deportation-of-slovak-jews, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Slovak National Uprising
claims.summary: The Slovak National Uprising broke out at Banská Bystrica against the Tiso regime and German occupation; after two months of fighting the rising was crushed on 27 October 1944 amid brutal reprisals.

sources.label: The Slovak National Uprising of 1944
sources.publisher: The National WWII Museum, New Orleans

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Slovakia: From Great Moravia to the heart of Europe, a nation that waited a thousand years for its own state.", terralore.co/country/SVK/chronicle#ev-1944-slovak-national-uprising, claim TL:SVK:event:1944:slovak-national-uprising, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Communist takeover
claims.summary: The Communist Party seized full power in Czechoslovakia, establishing a one-party state under Soviet domination that would last for four decades.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Slovakia: From Great Moravia to the heart of Europe, a nation that waited a thousand years for its own state.", terralore.co/country/SVK/chronicle#ev-1948-communist-takeover, claim TL:SVK:event:1948:communist-takeover, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Federalization of Czechoslovakia
claims.summary: After the Prague Spring was crushed, the Constitutional Law of Federation of 28 October 1968 created, from 1 January 1969, a Slovak Socialist Republic within a federal Czechoslovakia, the Slovaks' first republic in name.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Slovakia: From Great Moravia to the heart of Europe, a nation that waited a thousand years for its own state.", terralore.co/country/SVK/chronicle#ev-1968-federalization-of-czechoslovakia, claim TL:SVK:event:1968:federalization-of-czechoslovakia, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Velvet Revolution
claims.summary: Beginning with a student march in Bratislava on 16 November and protests in Prague the next day, six weeks of demonstrations led the Communist Party to give up its monopoly, ending one-party rule peacefully.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Slovakia: From Great Moravia to the heart of Europe, a nation that waited a thousand years for its own state.", terralore.co/country/SVK/chronicle#ev-1989-the-velvet-revolution, claim TL:SVK:event:1989:the-velvet-revolution, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Velvet Divorce
claims.summary: Czechoslovakia split peacefully into the Czech Republic and Slovakia on 1 January 1993, creating, after more than a thousand years, the first fully independent Slovak state.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Slovakia: From Great Moravia to the heart of Europe, a nation that waited a thousand years for its own state.", terralore.co/country/SVK/chronicle#ev-1993-the-velvet-divorce, claim TL:SVK:event:1993:the-velvet-divorce, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: ICJ judgment on Gabčíkovo–Nagymaros
claims.summary: The International Court of Justice ruled in the Gabčíkovo–Nagymaros Project case (Hungary/Slovakia) that both states had breached their obligations over the Danube dam treaty of 1977, ordering them to negotiate in good faith.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Slovakia: From Great Moravia to the heart of Europe, a nation that waited a thousand years for its own state.", terralore.co/country/SVK/chronicle#ev-1997-icj-judgment-on-gabcikovo-nagymaros, claim TL:SVK:event:1997:icj-judgment-on-gabcikovo-nagymaros, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Slovakia joins NATO
claims.summary: Slovakia officially became a member of NATO on 29 March 2004, part of the largest single enlargement in the Alliance's history, anchoring the young republic in the Western security community.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Slovakia: From Great Moravia to the heart of Europe, a nation that waited a thousand years for its own state.", terralore.co/country/SVK/chronicle#ev-2004-slovakia-joins-nato, claim TL:SVK:event:2004:slovakia-joins-nato, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Accession to the European Union
claims.summary: Slovakia joined the European Union on 1 May 2004, completing its integration into Western Europe little more than a decade after independence.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Slovakia: From Great Moravia to the heart of Europe, a nation that waited a thousand years for its own state.", terralore.co/country/SVK/chronicle#ev-2004-accession-to-the-european-union, claim TL:SVK:event:2004:accession-to-the-european-union, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Slovakia adopts the euro
claims.summary: Slovakia adopted the euro on 1 January 2009, becoming the sixteenth member of the euro area and the first of the Visegrád states to do so.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Slovakia: From Great Moravia to the heart of Europe, a nation that waited a thousand years for its own state.", terralore.co/country/SVK/chronicle#ev-2009-slovakia-adopts-the-euro, claim TL:SVK:event:2009:slovakia-adopts-the-euro, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.
